statements.notes: Judging this needs a semantic read of each capability name.
statements.quote: Name each capability for a cohesive system behavior that can own related requirements as the system evolves.

statements.notes: A rule can flag capability names that match proposal section headings; names that are really tasks need judgment.
statements.quote: Do not name implementation tasks or proposal sections.

statements.notes: A rule can catch names like 'misc', 'general' or 'core'.
Check each segment with a regex like ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$. Whether it fits the existing organization is checked only partially.
statements.quote: Use kebab-case for path segments you introduce (e.g., user-auth or identity/user-auth) that follow the project's existing spec organization.

statements.notes: Each modified capability must match an existing directory under openspec/specs/.
statements.quote: Use the exact existing path under openspec/specs/.

statements.notes: The section may be empty when existing requirements are not changing.
statements.quote: Leave empty if no requirement changes.

statements.notes: If both New and Modified Capabilities are empty, .openspec.yaml must contain skip_specs: true.
statements.quote: A change with no capabilities at all (pure refactor, tooling, docs) must set `skip_specs: true` in its .openspec.yaml - openspec validate rejects a zero-delta change without that marker.

statements.notes: Needs judgment about whether a requirement is real.
statements.quote: Do not invent a requirement just to satisfy validation.
